title: CWS After the LA Fires
subtitle: CWS’s response to the January 2025 fires: evacuation supplies, translated information and a shared registration system at the Wildfire Resource Hub.
excerpt: CWS’s response to the January 2025 fires: evacuation supplies, translated information and a shared registration system at the Wildfire Resource Hub.

content.alt: A CWS relief table with folded blankets and branded supply bags
content.caption: CWS blankets and bags at a wildfire relief station.

content.text: After the January 2025 fires in Los Angeles County, Church World Service (CWS) and its local offices packed more than 200 evacuation bags for newcomer families. The bags were fireproof and waterproof. Staff also helped families find temporary housing and get information in a language they could use.

I volunteered with CWS during the relief effort. One detail in its February 4 report caught my attention: in Pasadena, several relief organizations were working out how a family could register with all of them at once.

For six days, the Wildfire Resource Hub brought food, financial aid, counseling and housing assistance to one site. CWS translated disaster preparedness materials and supplied 5,000 bags with supplies and information for survivors. These were separate from the evacuation bags it had assembled for newcomer families.
The Hub was introducing an ID tag for each family. Someone who had described losing a home at one desk could show the tag at the next, instead of having to tell the story all over again.

content.alt: People and service tables in a courtyard beneath a Wildfire Resource Hub banner
content.caption: Assistance providers and families gather at the Wildfire Resource Hub.

content.text: CWS and California Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster asked a local Children’s Disaster Services team to spend a week at the Pasadena Hub. With someone there to look after their children, parents could talk to a housing worker or counselor nearby.

After the six days, people still needed somewhere to take a housing question. The Hub referred families to local providers for longer-term help. CWS worked with the Los Angeles County Long Term Recovery Group as well.
